Not a BFC; no background or border of its own. When content starts with a

end marker are non-floated fit-content blocks, not BFCs: beside a LEFT widget wider than the label, the box starts at the column edge, its one line cannot fit beside the float, and the text is pushed below the widget (CSS 2.1 9.5), detaching the model label from the content; the box then spans the widget's height and, because the block paints in the positioned layer, its 1px border-right (border-left for the marker) is likely drawn as a vertical line over the widget (inferred; verify). Painting: position:relative + opacity .94 make a stacking context in the positioned layer, so EVERYTHING inside paints above a non-positioned widget float outside it (nested quote bar, bare pre box, collapsible rule, list markers), and the block likely takes clicks over the overlapped part of the widget (inferred). blocks.layoutFacts: clear:left/right makes floats on the same side stack vertically. A left and a right float can sit side by side, but each wrap test uses the whole column and ignores the other float, so the text between them can be narrower than 300px. The .iframe-widget div is a zero-height normal block (its only child floats), so the float spills into following blocks. Reader BFC root: the MultiToCLayout grid cell div.content (components/posts/TableOfContents/MultiToCLayout.tsx:23, 258), so a float near the end hangs past the last block but stays in that cell. A px-width widget does not scale, so it floats at some window widths and is full width at others. Load sequence: useColumnWidth is null in SSR and the first render (HydratedIframeWidget.tsx:12-24), so the widget renders full width first and floats only after measuring (layout shift); the iframe starts at 400px until its resize message, so the float height and which lines wrap change after load. The float is not positioned, so positioned or stacking-context neighbours paint above it and take its clicks. The iframe has no background (transparent unless the widget HTML sets one; a color-scheme mismatch may paint an opaque canvas, verify in dark mode). shape-outside changes only line wrapping: BFC boxes and clear still use the full margin box including the empty pushed area. Vertical editor/post drift: the sentinels' line boxes block margin collapsing, so the editor gap between the paragraphs around a top-level widget is about 2em vs 1em in the post (the empty div's margins collapse through); the float top is p_bottom + 1em + 6px in both, so the paragraph after a top-aligned widget starts about 1em lower relative to the widget in the editor and different lines wrap beside it; nothing compensates (inferred from Editor.tsx:288-290; verify). align=bottom breaks when the next block cannot sit beside the widget: alignedParagraph takes the next sibling of ANY type at least 1px tall (bottomAlign.ts:9-13) and the gear menu offers Bottom whatever follows (WidgetOptionsMenu.tsx:131-132). If that block is placed below the float (h1/h2 in the post or h1-h3 in the editor, hr, post table, 100%-wide embed iframe, the editor's image flex container, a full-width widget), each push moves it down too, the gap never closes, alignFloatBottom keeps the largest of 6 tries with gap >= -1 (bottomAlign.ts:36-52), so the widget ends up pushed down ~5x its first gap with a blank band above; later re-runs start from the stored push (35) and can push further (inferred; verify). Next blocks that wrap or narrow converge (paragraphs, lists, code blocks, the editor table wrapper, Estimaker/Viewpoints). Editor: the overlay is absolute with z-index 1, so the widget always paints above its neighbours there; none of the reader's 'neighbour paints over the widget' collisions appear in the editor.

In an RTL list the UA padding-inline-start (40px/level) and outside markers move right, repeating the list problem mirrored beside a RIGHT float (nesting collapses, markers near or over the widget); the paragraph indent (padding-inline-start, Lexical.dev.mjs:9835-9837) also moves right. dir=auto on a list or quote takes the first strong character's direction for all items. The post shows the same text LTR, so RTL content wraps differently around a widget in the editor and the post.
